records.name: Double Trellis Food Initiative
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that cooks meals for people in need, including unhoused neighbors, and gives them to partner programs. It also runs a four-month culinary training program for young adults who were formerly incarcerated.
records.what_you_do: News coverage from 2024 and 2025 says the group cooks meals, hands them to partner programs and community fridges, and runs its training program with a partner. Its website returned a not found error when checked, and no volunteer shift or donation drop-off is described on any page we could open, so confirm how to help before you plan a visit.

first_step.how: Check doubletrellis.org for a volunteer or donation page before planning a visit. The site returned a not found error on 2026-10-08, so confirm the group is still taking help first.
first_step.basis: No volunteer shift, orientation or drop in visit is described on any page we could open, and the group's own website was not available, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pages we could open do not describe a visit or a volunteer shift. News coverage from 2024 says the group cooks about 300 meals a day and sends them to partner programs and community fridges that serve people who are unhoused or in need.

records.notes: Both doubletrellis.org and www.doubletrellis.org returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-08, so volunteer and donation paths remain unconfirmed. The Philly Daily page shows an update date of May 15, 2026; that is a page update rather than group news, so it is not used as activity evidence. The 2024 feature says the four-month training runs with YEAH Philly; that partner was not checked. The IRS data lists two ZIP codes (19134 and 19125) for the same street address; both are carried over unchanged. Search: one search, which found no current volunteer page.

records.name: Harriett's Bookclub
records.summary: A Philadelphia book club run by its own nonprofit. It hosts author talks, book events, dinners and essay club nights, but its website does not post regular meeting dates or a book list.
records.what_you_do: Takes part in the club's author talks, book events, dinners and essay club, which the events page lists. The site does not say how the club's own meetings work, so email to ask how to attend.

first_step.how: Email hello@harriettsbook.club to ask when the next book club meeting or event is, where it meets, and whether new people can come.
first_step.basis: The events page lists many public events, but it does not say when or where the book club meets or who can attend, so the way in is an email first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. Its events page lists past author talks, book events, a dinner tied to a book, and an essay club held on February 18, 2026, with no prices or meeting times shown. Ask by email what the next event is and whether it is open to people new to the club.
first_visit_tips: Email rather than using the newsletter sign up, which the site says is not set up yet.

records.notes: The events page lists 21 events from September 2021 to February 18, 2026, most of them in the past. It does not say whether events are open to the public or list prices. The newest dated listing is February 2026, which moves status from probably_active to active. The 2021 listings place events at Harriett's Bookshop at 258 East Girard Avenue, the same street address as the IRS record; that older listing is not used as the current location. The home page gives ZIP 91215, which looks like a typo, so it is not used. The newsletter sign up says it needs a storage option. A merchandise store link and a sponsor line on the vision page were not followed.

records.name: Meraki Animal Sanctuary
records.summary: A registered nonprofit animal sanctuary that cares for animals in need until they can go to permanent homes. Volunteers can foster cats, including mother cats and kittens, through its foster program.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat, a litter, or a friendly stray for a short stay in your home. The sanctuary provides a starter kit, and you can also adopt through the Adopt page or donate supplies or money for vet visits. The site does not describe general volunteer shifts.

cost.text: The site lists no fees for fostering. It asks for donations and says fosters receive a starter kit.

first_step.how: Open the Foster Care Application from the Foster Care page at merakianimalsanctuary.com/foster-care, or email merakianimalsanctuary@gmail.com with questions first.
first_step.basis: Fostering starts with an application, though the sanctuary offers help with questions along the way, so there is a step to complete before you can start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Fostering is described as short term. You care for a mother cat with kittens, orphan kittens, or a friendly adult stray, and the sanctuary provides a starter kit with food, a litter box, litter, bowls, a carrier and a few toys. The page does not give a stay length, housing rules, or any training step.

records.notes: The foster page's application button has no visible link, so no application URL is recorded. The foster page gives no stay length, age limits, housing rules, or orientation. The home page newsletter sign up carries a note that it needs a storage location. The About page has no dates, hours, or volunteer roles. The Adopt and Donate pages were not read. Status stays probably_active because no dated news was found on the pages read.

records.name: Athletic Base Ball Club of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit club that plays and teaches base ball the way it was played in the 1860s. It puts on live games and demonstrations for the public, and it welcomes new players and umpires.
records.what_you_do: Play in period style games, umpire them (the club calls its umpires arbiters), or join as a non-playing supporting member who backs the club's mission.

schedule.text: No recurring schedule is posted yet. The club says times and places will be added to its schedule as they are set.

cost.text: No membership fee is listed on the site. New members get a first year discount, but no amount is given. Uniform costs are in a linked document that did not open when checked.

requirements.gear: A club uniform, as set out in the club's uniform regulations (the document did not open when checked).

first_step.how: Email info@phillyvintagebaseball.org or use the contact form on the club's site to ask about playing, umpiring, or joining as a supporting member.
first_step.basis: The club says interest is the only requirement to play or umpire, has a join section with a contact form, and welcomes players, umpires and supporting members. No game dates or practice times are posted yet.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. It says the club stages live games and demonstrations for the public, but no dates are posted yet, so ask by email whether something is coming up and where it will be.
first_visit_tips: Follow the club on social media, since the site sends people there for game dates.
Ask about the uniform rules before buying anything, since the club links a uniform regulations document.

records.notes: No game or demonstration dates were posted at check time, so no dated event is recorded. The news section is an embedded feed with no visible dated items. The uniform regulations document is a Google Drive file that showed only a loading screen, so uniform costs and rules are unconfirmed. Tier one said membership costs were listed on the site; the join section names no fee, so the cost text is corrected. The sitemap date is the only dated evidence and is a file date rather than a news item, so status stays probably_active. The merchandise store (third party) was not followed.

records.name: Here Kitty Kitty Cat Rescue
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that rescues homeless and unwanted cats and places them in permanent homes, with help from volunteers and donors.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can foster cats and kittens, help with transport, help with fundraising or social media, or join a street team that asks shops to host a cat in the window. You can also adopt a cat or kitten, donate, or send items from the wish lists. The Get Involved page lists the volunteer and foster steps.

schedule.text: No events are listed. The events page says no current events were found when checked.

cost.text: Adoption fees and donation amounts are on the adoption and donate pages and were not recorded.

first_step.how: Send the volunteer or foster application from the Get Involved page at herekittykitty.org, or email info@herekittykitty.org, which the rescue says it usually answers within 24 hours.
first_step.basis: Volunteering and fostering both start with an application form, and the site lists no orientation or meeting times, so the way in needs a step first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe an orientation, shift times, or a visiting day. Listed roles include fostering, where the rescue covers medical care, food and litter as needed, plus fundraising, social media, transport, and a street team that asks shops to host a cat in their window.
first_visit_tips: Email info@herekittykitty.org if the form is unclear, since the rescue usually replies within 24 hours.
Ask about shelter hours and any visiting rules before you travel, because the site does not list them.

records.notes: The Get Involved page gives one form link for both foster and volunteer applications. The events page shows no current events. Home page news items carry only a month and day (July 30, December 9 and December 19) with no year, so they are not dated evidence and status stays probably_active. The home page says the rescue was formerly Zoomies Animal Rescue; not added as an alias, for the owner to decide. The IRS record gives ZIP 19146 while the site's mailing line says 19134; the IRS location is carried over unchanged. Two IRS rows for the same address (spelled Frnt and Front) were merged into one. The Adoption and Donate pages were not read. Wish list links were not followed.

records.name: Kitten Snatchers
records.summary: A volunteer-run Philadelphia rescue that takes in stray cats and kittens and places them in foster homes until they are adopted.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat in your home while it waits for adoption, or offer temporary hosting. Adopt through the online application, or donate. The rescue has no shelter building, so cats live with volunteer fosters.

schedule.text: No recurring events or hours are listed on the site.

cost.text: Adoption fees are $155 for cats over 1 year, $180 for cats under 1 year, and $500 for purebreds, which the site says include tax. The site says the fee covers spay or neuter, medical care, and foster care, and it lists no fee for fostering.

first_step.how: Fill in the foster application or the temporary host form linked on the site, or email cats@kittensnatchers.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Fostering, hosting and adopting all start with a form, and the site lists no orientation, volunteer shifts, or events, so the way in is a form first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adopters apply online, and approval can take up to 5 days. The rescue then connects you with the foster caring for the cat, you meet by video or in person, and kittens go home only after spay or neuter surgery. The pages read do not describe foster duties, supplies, orientation, or hours.
first_visit_tips: Pick at least two cats you like, since the adoption page advises it in case another adopter gets the first one.
Expect the foster to ask about your home life and what you want in a cat.

records.notes: The adoption page gives the rescue's regular adoption fees, which the page says include tax. The one-time Clear the Shelters promotion (August 1 to 31, 2026, with reduced fees) was removed from schedule text because promotions do not belong there; it remains the newest dated evidence for status and last sign of life. The footer copyright and the founding year on the About page were not treated as dated evidence. Payment details on the adoption page were not recorded. The Google Forms linked for adoption, foster and temporary host were not opened. No hours or street address are published. The IRS rows for 164 Sigel St (spelled Street and St) were merged into one.

records.name: MARX Inc Youth Services
records.summary: A youth services group that supports teens with leadership, mentoring, and scholarships to help them grow into adult leaders.
records.what_you_do: Leadership workshops that build life skills, teen mentoring that connects young people with networking and positive relationships, and scholarships with service learning. The site does not say how a teen enrolls or how to volunteer, so email to ask.

schedule.text: No program dates or schedule are published on the site.

cost.text: Not published. The site invites donations through its Donate page.

first_step.how: Email marxincyouth@gmail.com, or send a message through the contact form on the group's Contact page, to ask how a teen joins its leadership, mentoring or scholarship programs.
first_step.basis: Three programs are named, but the site does not say how a teen or parent enrolls, so the way in is a question to the group first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes leadership workshops, teen mentoring, and scholarships with service learning, but it gives no dates, places, or costs for any of them. A visit or enrollment would be arranged through the group by email or its contact form.

records.notes: The site footer reads 2021 and no dated program notice or news item was found on the three pages read, so status stays probably_active on the working site alone. The About page gives no age range, neighborhood, or enrollment steps; the teen focus comes from the mentoring text. The Donate page and the Facebook page were not read. Confidence is low: nothing on the site is dated after 2021, and email is the only way in that was confirmed.

blocked.note: Group website returned not found on 2026-10-08. Tier one also could not load it.
Same site without www, also not found on 2026-10-08.
Athletic Base Ball uniform regulations file. Showed only a loading screen and a sign in link, so unreadable.

notes: Seven records, all verdict publish, tier 2 deep pass. Fetches used 24 of the 60 cap (never more than 6 per group). Searches used 1 of 1. Double Trellis: both doubletrellis.org addresses returned 404 on 2026-10-08, so its volunteer and donation paths are unconfirmed; status stays probably_active from the April 2025 news story. Harriett's Bookclub moved from probably_active to active on a February 2026 events listing. Kitten Snatchers' promotion text was moved out of schedule text. Leads: none listed. Partner names were dropped with reasons rather than listed: YEAH Philly, Northwest Mutual Aid Collective, Sharing Excess, Sharefood and Carversville Farm Foundation appear only in a news feature about Double Trellis (not checked; the foundation is likely a private foundation, out of scope); Penn Treaty SSD appears only as a sponsor line on Harriett's vision page (not checked, not shown to be a joinable group); ACCT, the shelter named on Kitten Snatchers' About page, is a shelter rather than a volunteer group and was not checked. Kitten Snatchers' Google Forms and the Here Kitty application form were not opened. Duplicate IRS location rows were merged where they were the same address spelled differently.
